content:
**Observations:**
- Two dried stems, gray to whitish in color
- Dense covering of tiny black specks across the entire stem surface
- The speckled pattern looks like scattered charcoal dust/microsclerotia
- No white fluffy mold, no lesions with defined borders, no foliar tissue visible

**Reasoning:**
The defining feature is the gray stem surface covered uniformly with tiny black specks. This matches Charcoal Rot exactly: "stems near soil surface appear gray with tiny black specks or dots resembling charcoal dust" and "small black spots (pycnidia/microsclerotia) irregularly dispersed across stem surface." The lower stem in the image is particularly white-gray with black speckling — the hallmark appearance of *Macrophomina phaseolina*.

White Mold could show gray stems but would have white cottony growth and embedded sclerotia (larger, visible black bodies), not uniformly scattered fine specks. Anthracnose has acervuli with setae and is more associated with pods/petioles. Neither fits as well as Charcoal Rot.
